edit.explain.motion: A crank-rocker four-bar O2-A-B-O4 has a triangular coupler, and its point P traces an egg-shaped coupler curve. One side of that curve is very nearly a circular arc of radius 61.5 mm. A link PD of exactly that length ties P to the output rocker O6-D. While P runs along the arc, D sits at the arc's centre and does not move, so the output stands within 1° for about 90° of crank turn. For the rest of the turn the curve leaves the arc, PD pushes D away, and the output swings 69° out and back.
edit.build.defining_relations: Four-bar Grashof: 30 + 87 <= 57 + 72, so the crank turns fully. P is at (9, -32) from A, x along AB. Dwell rule: PD = e equals the radius of the near-circular arc of P's curve (61.5 mm), and D's rest position (20.2, -58.4) is that arc's centre; |P - D rest| stays 60.9 to 61.5 mm over the dwell. Output rocker O6D = 40. Mobility 3(6-1)-2*7 = 1. Stephenson III: the dyad runs from the coupler to ground.

edit.build.defining_relations: R = 2r (zr = 2 zp). Planet absolute rotation = -(zr/zp - 1) x arm angle = -u. A point on the planet pitch circle that starts at (R, 0) is at x = R cos(u), y = 0, so it moves on a straight diameter with simple harmonic motion. The opposite end of that planet diameter, which starts at O, moves on y = R sin(u): tracer Y. In general a pitch point at angle alpha round the planet from X runs on the ring diameter at alpha/2, so the two lines at right angles come from the two ends of one planet diameter. Points at radius rho < r trace ellipses with semi-axes r + rho and r - rho.

review.note: Applies the 2026-10-19 review and #213 (rethink). The canonical layout: the rod lies on top, the two blocks run in the plate's crossed grooves and are pinned up into it, and the pen is at the rod's end, so the rod and both blocks read as one bar riding two slides. Changed in the build (R2): the crank turns under the blocks on a shaft from the base, its pin M rising through the groove plate's open middle to the rod's midpoint, instead of a crank above the rod driven from a bridge: the builder holds a driven shaft from the base only, and the crank under the plate leaves the rod, the blocks and the pen on top in plain view. The groove plate replaces each slide's rails (teaching.exceptions). The pen's distances to the two blocks are drawn as the ellipse's half-axes; ghost traces for the pen at the midpoint (a circle) and at block Y (a straight line) show the family.

edit.explain.motion: One block slides along the horizontal groove and the other along the vertical one. A rod lies on top of both and is pinned to each, and a crank from the crossing to the rod's midpoint turns it round. The blocks pass through the crossing one at a time, and a pen at the rod's end traces an ellipse whose half-axes are its distances to the two blocks.
edit.explain.limits: Sliders need clean, low-play grooves or the ellipse distorts. The blocks must cross the middle of the plate, so both grooves are cut through one plate and meet there; the rod rides above the plate on the blocks' pins, and the crank turns under the plate, its pin rising through the open middle to the rod.
edit.build.ground: one cross-shaped groove plate (a + sign, both grooves meeting at O, open round the middle where the crank pin runs) on the base; the crank shaft comes up at O from the base, under the plate
edit.build.notes: Crank and rod turn in opposite senses (rod angle = -θ). Layout (rethink, #213): the rod on top, the two blocks in the plate's grooves and pinned up into it, the pen at the rod's end; the crank under the blocks, its pin rising through the plate's open middle to the rod's midpoint. The groove plate stays and is drawn see-through where it covers a block or the rod. The crank to the midpoint duplicates a constraint the blocks already give (overconstrained).
edit.topology.notes: ground with crossed grooves, two blocks, rod, and a drive crank to the rod midpoint; count includes ground. Overconstrained: the crank repeats a constraint the two blocks already give, so Gruebler counts 0 but the trammel moves with 1 dof
